bib.title: The Dawn of GUI Agent: A Preliminary Case Study with Claude 3.5 Computer Use

question: What can Claude 3.5 Computer Use, the first frontier API-based GUI agent, and cannot do on real desktop tasks across web, office, workflow and game software, judged on planning, action and critic?
contributions: A case study of Claude 3.5 Computer Use on desktop task automation covering web search, professional software and games
An out-of-the-box, cross-platform (Windows/macOS, Docker-free) agent framework, Computer Use OOTB, for deploying API-based GUI automation models
Human evaluations and analyses of advances and limitations, with a Planning/Action/Critic error taxonomy

method.summary: Authors hand-wrote user queries and initial states for a set of desktop tasks, ran Claude 3.5 Computer Use on real Windows and macOS machines through their PyAutoGUI-based OOTB framework, and manually judged the final state of each run as Success or Failed. Each run is narrated by planning, action and critic; four failures are analysed.
method.task: GUI desktop task automation from natural-language instruction using screenshots only

limits: Preliminary case study: about 19-20 hand-picked tasks, one run each, no baseline model, no benchmark, no aggregate success rate.
Success judged manually by the authors on the final state; no inter-rater check or criteria beyond that.
Only Claude 3.5 Computer Use (October 2024 beta) is tested; the authors call for more dynamic benchmarks that track software versions.
No decoding settings, step caps, token/cost or latency numbers reported.
Task set skews to successes; failures are 4 of 19 and each analysed from a single trace.
Games tested are turn-based only; real-time action games are excluded.
Likely dated: the model is the first public beta; later computer-use models and benchmarks supersede it.
Authors concede page scrolling via Page Up/Down and critic over-confidence are unresolved.
